note: Item wording transcribed from the PLOS article's Table 1 'Items of the scales' (Self-congruity [SELFCON] block, Sirgy et al. 1997), which PLOS publishes only as an IMAGE -- read from the .t001 PNG (same image batch_089/090/436 used), so the transcription is a fallible image read and worth a character-level human spot-check. Item 4 is kept verbatim as printed: 'how I like be seen by others' (the source omits 'to'); not corrected. None of the four items is quoted verbatim in the article prose; the prose (section on self-congruity) gives Sirgy's generic product/brand examples in the order actual self, ideal self, social self, ideal social self, whereas Table 1's bullets read actual, social, ideal, ideal social -- the Table 1 order is the one shipped. The four SELFCON bullets are unnumbered, so bullet order was taken as the SELFCON1..SELFCON4 numbering Table 2 uses; hence mapping_basis=paper_order. CODE DERIVATION: data/lunacortes_2019_vsn_scales.py lowercases and replaces '-' in 'Self-Cong1'..'Self-Cong4' to give self_cong1..self_cong4, melting BY NAME (no positional step); confirmed cell-for-cell, all four live items identical to their namesake S1 columns over 444 respondents. MAPPING EVIDENCE (Step 5b, PARTIAL): live 4-item alpha 0.7245 reproduces published 0.724 (block identity). Table 2 loadings 0.73/0.72/0.95/0.95 predict {3,4} strongest, {1,2} weakest; live 1-factor loadings 0.570/0.503/0.715/0.740 and corrected item-total r 0.4836/0.4453/0.5711/0.5636 match that split on both. NOT ESTABLISHED: order within {1,2} and within {3,4} (published loadings tied/near-tied); those rest on bullet order alone. ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: interviews in Spanish (section 3.2) with a four-step forward translation from English (section 3.3); no Spanish wording is published -- the sole supplement S1 File is the response XLSX (sheet Hoja1) with bare code headers and no Spanish item text, and the article prints English only. Fallback: English in base fields, language=Spanish, empty _translated columns, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. Section 3.3 notes some verbs were replaced with easier Spanish synonyms after pre-test, so the administered Spanish is not a strict rendering of this English. SCALE ANCHORS: only endpoints labelled ('from 1-totally disagree, to 7-totally agree', section 3.2); resp 2-6 option_text left blank, not padded. No instructions printed, so instructions blank. STEP 3b: clean -- 4 items on resp 1-7 matches the Table 1 SELFCON block and the dictionary Description; column names pin the block (Self-Cong vs IC/ISNCC, also 4 items). RIGHTS: wording from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article; Sirgy et al. (1997) has no row in instrument_rights_register.csv and no fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause was located, so silence-is-permission applies. No register row written. COVERAGE: 4 items x 7 resp levels (28 rows); n=444 per item; every item uses all seven levels.

note: item_text is the .sav's own SPSS variable label for each column and option_text its value labels, transcribed verbatim (straight quotes kept; nothing normalised); instructions blank because neither the file nor the paper prints any. CODE DERIVATION: item IS the source column name (data/lee_2020_medical_students.py melts Drinking_habit_1..3 unchanged), so there is no mapping step. RESP: the processing script exports the .sav's stored codes as-is (pd.to_numeric, no recode), and the live table's item x resp counts match the .sav's value counts cell for cell, 15/15 nonzero cells (e.g. Drinking_habit_1 213/326/131/37/10; Drinking_habit_2 289/311/83/25/4/3; Drinking_habit_3 523/150/35/6/1); the live table has 717 ids against 746 .sav rows, the difference being respondents missing all three items. WORDING: this is a past-year, past-tense AUDIT-C variant with a standard-drink definition appended to item 1 (as used in US college AUDIT-C forms; the paper cites Wahesh & Lewis 2015 and Bush et al. 1998), not the WHO AUDIT's present-tense wording. Item 1's top category reads '4-5 times a week', not the canonical '4 or more times a week' -- shipped as the file has it; the paper also speaks of '4-5 times per week'. Drinking_habit_2 has SIX categories and the live resp is the category index (0 drinks=0 ... 10 or more drinks=5), NOT AUDIT-C points: the paper scores '0 drinks' and '1-2 drinks' both as 0 (the .sav's drinking_habit_2_transform), so resp 0-5 here are not AUDIT points for that item. LANGUAGE: English. The paper names no administration language; the .sav has 0 CJK characters across all variable and value labels, and the survey was of CUHK medical students (English-medium programme), so the English labels are taken as the administered wording. RIGHTS -- per instrument_rights_register.csv row 'Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT)', verdict ship_with_note (Ben, 2026-09-19): THE ITEMS DERIVE FROM WHO's AUDIT, and WHO is credited: Babor, Higgins-Biddle, Saunders & Monteiro, 'AUDIT: The Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test -- Guidelines for Use in Primary Care', 2nd ed., WHO/MSD/MSB/01.6a (2001), iris.who.int/handle/10665/67205. Its copyright page reads: 'This document is not a formal publication of the World Health Organization (WHO), and all rights are reserved by the Organization. The document may, however, be freely reviewed, abstracted, reproduced, and translated, in part or in whole but not for sale or for use in conjunction with commercial purposes.' Why that does not block: it grants free non-commercial reproduction rather than reserving a permission gate; the 'inquiries should be addressed to' sentence after it concerns new editions and translations; IRW is non-commercial; no WHO endorsement is implied and no WHO logo is reproduced. The register row was applied, not re-derived. The wording shipped here is the study's own English adaptation (past-year) taken from its CC BY deposit.
public_note: AUDIT-C in a past-year wording from the study's own data file. For Drinking_habit_2 the response values are the questionnaire's six categories in order (0 = 0 drinks ... 5 = 10 or more drinks), not AUDIT-C points -- standard scoring gives both '0 drinks' and '1-2 drinks' 0 points -- and Drinking_habit_1's highest category is '4-5 times a week' rather than the standard '4 or more times a week'.
